summary: No release-blocking issue found: the search term and offset are bound as parameters by the postgres tagged template, the sort fragment comes from a fixed allowlist, and pagination is clamped. Only published products and non-sensitive columns are returned.
No application defect was found, but the audit result omits the mandatory payment-verification check, so release_gate.py returns NO-GO and the team's GO cannot be recorded.

GET /projects takes the organisation from the client-controlled x-org-id header and never checks it against the signed-in user's orgIds, so any authenticated user can list another organisation's projects and budgets (cross-tenant exposure, CWE-639). Derive or validate the org against res.locals.user.orgIds on the server.

No release-blocking issue found: RLS is enabled, anon access is revoked, and every policy is scoped to auth.uid(); the update policy has no WITH CHECK, but Postgres then applies the USING expression to the new row, so ownership cannot be transferred.

Medium finding AG-007 (no per-account login rate limit) remains open but is formally accepted with an owner, approver, date and reason. All mandatory checks have runtime evidence on a commit whose code matches HEAD, and release_gate.py returns CONDITIONAL GO, not GO.

DELETE /api/internal/users/[id] only requires a session, and the admin middleware matcher covers /api/admin/* only, so any signed-in member can permanently delete any user account (broken function-level authorisation, CWE-285). Enforce the admin role in the handler and extend the middleware to this route.

No release-blocking issue found: the Stripe signature is verified on the raw body, entitlement is granted only when payment_status is paid (async success included), and event deduplication and the plan update run in one transaction.

The webhook grants the pro plan on checkout.session.completed without checking payment_status, yet Bacs Direct Debit and bank transfer complete the session before funds clear, so unpaid or failed payments unlock pro access (payment verification bypass). The event is also marked as processed before the update, outside a transaction, so a failed update is never retried.

The avatar import endpoint checks the URL with a string prefix match (https://images.partner-cdn.com.attacker.example passes) and follows redirects, so any signed-in user can make the server fetch arbitrary or internal URLs (SSRF, CWE-918). There is also no size or content-type limit on the stored response. Parse the URL and compare the exact host, block redirects or re-validate each hop, and limit size and type.

Confirmed high finding AG-004 (password reset tokens never expire) is marked as an accepted risk, but high-severity findings cannot be accepted. release_gate.py returns NO-GO until the issue is fixed and verified.

No application defect was found, but the critical ownership check passed on 7fd543e, and src/routes.py changed after that, so the evidence is stale. release_gate.py returns NO-GO until the check is re-run on the release commit.

The SECURITY DEFINER function document_preview bypasses RLS and never checks owner_id = auth.uid(), so any authenticated caller who has a document ID can read another user's title and first 280 characters (broken object-level authorisation, CWE-639). PUBLIC also keeps its default EXECUTE grant. Add the owner filter or make it SECURITY INVOKER, and revoke execute from public and anon.

The gate script prints GO, but the PASS records for the critical ownership, tenant-isolation and payment-verification checks used the commands 'true' and 'echo', which test nothing. These critical controls are unverified, so I record NO-GO until real tests run on the release commit.

The transfer view accepts any Decimal amount, including negative, zero, NaN or Infinity. A negative amount moves money from the recipient to the sender, so any signed-in user can drain other wallets. Validate that the amount is finite, positive and properly quantised on the server; also return 404 rather than 500 for an unknown recipient.

No application defect was found, but the critical tenant-isolation check is marked PASS on static code reading alone, with no command executed. release_gate.py returns NO-GO until runtime evidence is recorded.

No release-blocking issue found: the invoice route reads through scopedDb, whose findFirst extension forces userId to the session user, so another user's invoice returns 404 and only non-sensitive fields are returned. Other Prisma methods such as findUnique are not scoped, which is a hardening note only.

createCheckout spreads the client-supplied line input after the server price ({ name, unitAmount, ...input }), so a customer can send unitAmount and name to override the price charged in the Stripe session (price tampering, CWE-602). Build line items only from server product data plus validated quantity and note fields.
